lines: That was blunt enough to disappoint an arrow.
I have seen crooked shots with more sense than that.
A loose feather has softer manners than you.
Even a broken shaft knows when to stop.
You missed the point from two steps away.
I have seen bent arrows fly straighter than that thought.
Your manners need a better spine.
That confidence has poor aim and worse balance.
You are all tension and no control.
I would not trust that idea downrange.
A dull arrowhead has more edge than you just showed.
You make the target look quick witted.
Your sense drifts worse than feathers in a storm.
That remark landed sideways and snapped.
Even a bad shot teaches more than you did.
I could straighten a branch before straightening your logic.
You are the warning I give apprentices before practice.
That thought should have stayed in the quiver.
A loose string has better restraint.
You miss the point even when nobody is shooting at you.
Keep testing my patience and you will learn how warnings travel.
Stay where I can see your hands.
Take one more step and this talk is over.
I am listening, but I am not lowering my guard.
Say what you came to say from there.
Do not bring your trouble near my workshop.
The village has had enough of you for one day.
I remember last time. That is why the bow is ready.
You can leave quietly or explain yourself quickly.
I am trying to end this without ringing the bell.
Keep your voice down and your distance longer.
Trust does not grow back as quickly as an arrow shaft.
One wrong move and everyone at the gate will know.
I would rather return to work than trade threats with you.
Nothing about your tone makes me want you closer.
I am not afraid of you. I am tired of your trouble.
There are twenty arrows behind me and no reason to waste one.
If you came for a fight, keep walking.
You have one chance to make this conversation useful.
Leave the threats outside the village.
